chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorced woman beautifies herself for her husband as long as he has the right of reversion (raj'ah) upon her, and he does not need permission to go to her.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Right of reversion (the husband's right to take back his wife during Iddah without a new contract)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights and duties of a divorced woman during the waiting period of a revocable divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the status of a woman in the 'Iddah of a revocable divorce (Taliq Raj'i), emphasizing her readiness to return to her husband who holds the unilateral right of retraction (Ruj'u). It highlights the practical implication that the husband may resume marital relations without requiring her explicit consent or a new marriage contract, reflecting the temporary nature of this divorce phase in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The divorced woman should yearn (beautify herself) for her husband for as long as there is reversion for him upon her, and he does not need permission to go to her’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A woman who is divorced and her husband has the right to go back to her, can beautify herself before her husband and he does not need to ask permission to go to her.’”
